judged_text: addMembers leaves the TODO 'should clear the input' unimplemented, so the user-selector retains its usernames after a successful add. An admin who clicks 'Add' twice (or clicks Add after editing the list) re-submits the same username list; combined with the silent per-username add loop, stale input makes it easy to fire repeated add requests without noticing.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the new `addMembers` action explicitly leaves `// TODO: should clear the input` and only calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without clearing/resetting `usernames` afterward. From the diff we can verify the input value is not cleared, so the selector can retain the previous usernames and a subsequent click would re-submit the same list. The claim about “silent per-username add loop” is also supported by the server-side `add_members` action looping `usernames.split(",").each` and not reporting per-username results. This is a concrete UX/behavior concern, but the diff does not prove it causes incorrect membership state (e.g., duplicates) because `group.add(user)` idempotency/error behavior isn’t shown here.
